newsitem.title: USA: Lund Q1 hurt by fiberglass program.
newsitem.headline: Lund Q1 hurt by fiberglass program.

text.p: Lund International Holdings Inc said Monday first quarter net income declined due to the implementation of a new quality program in the fiberglass manufacturing area, which reduced output during the initial stage.
It also cited higher than expected warranty expense.
Earlier, Lund reported earnings for the first quarter ended September 30 of $0.11 a share, down from $0.22.
Lund also said marketing expenses and research and development costs increased in the quarter, partly due to new technology including three-dimensional design software and hardware.
Lund, which makes appearance accessories for new and used light trucks, said the new technology is designed to increase productivity once the initial training phase is complete.

"Lund's segment of the automotive aftermarket industry is strengthening and internal improvements have put Lund in a position to capitalize on the opportunities available," William McMahon, president, said in a statement. "We have added new products and improved the quality of existing lines. We are in the process of reducing manufacturing costs."
